_comment: Editorial rules handed to every agent. Seeded from GDD section 10.2 —
Max's own editorial standards (rules 001-005 verbatim; 006 adapted from
the GDD's human-review standard into an instruction aimed at the model
that will be read by that reviewer) — plus four rules carried over
from the retired prototype crew (source 'prototype-crew'), each of which
exists because a live run produced the bad board it describes. Adopted
with Max on 2026-08-03 rather than rediscovered across thirty reviews;
the cases are recorded in the handbook at
Rules compiled from Max's recorded feedback land here after each batch of
the review loop, with source 'feedback-batch-N' and provenance naming the
runs and tags that justified them. Only status 'approved' rules are ever
loaded into a prompt, so a proposal can wait here without taking effect.

rules.text: Every pair in a set must share the same relationship.
The relationship label should make the answer feel fair once revealed.
A puzzle should avoid accidental alternate solutions unless intentionally designed for them.
Words should be familiar enough that the challenge is the relationship, not obscure vocabulary.
Hard puzzles can be abstract, but they should not be arbitrary.
A human editor reviews and edits every board before it is used; write for that reader.

A pair must be directional and transformative: B is an entity or outcome that A maps to, never a static adjective or property. "Caterpillar : Butterfly" and "Grape : Wine" work; "Gulf Stream : warm" does not.

provenance.note: a live run produced "Gulf Stream : warm"
provenance.retirement: Eliminated by Max 2026-08-04 (design.md D-3). The word 'transformative' overreached: read literally it forbade Brush : Painter, Nest : Bird and Dove : Peace — three of the four sets on the approved First Light board — and the whole arrowless class rated best in the two blind experiments (experiments/four-family-board, experiments/arrow-round-2). Likely the mechanical cause of ~80% of all authored pairs being one-thing-becomes-another. Its real intent — no static adjectives, B must be a thing — is enforced by the controlled shape vocabulary, which contains no adjective-shaped relation types.

rules.text: Both pairs in a set must share the same relationship type at the same grain. "Sonar : mapping :: Submersible : exploration" fails: a concrete process is being matched to a broad activity.

provenance.note: the sonar/submersible board matched a concrete process to a broad activity

rules.text: Never build a set from a progression chain that repeats a word, such as "Second : Minute :: Minute : Hour". A set is two independent pairs and needs four distinct words, so use "Second : Minute :: Hour : Day" instead. The same rule forbids a shared subject, which is the easier trap on a board about one person or place: "President : Air Force One :: President : Marine One" repeats a word just as surely, and needs a second subject — "President : Air Force One :: Monarch : royal train".

provenance.note: the Time and Music runs both produced progression chains; the shared-subject clause added 2026-08-06 after the Obama run failed terminally — 01 authored President/President, Obama/Obama and Cabinet secretary/Cabinet secretary, 02 grouped each with its twin, and three of seven candidate sets were illegal on the same word

rules.text: No word may plausibly belong to a second set. Before proposing a board, check whether any four of its words form another valid analogy; if they do, change the words.

provenance.note: the Adversarial Solver exists to hunt these

rules.text: B must follow from A necessarily, not occasionally. If there is a common case where A happens and B does not, the pair is broken. "Telescope : Discovery" fails this test — a telescope does not necessarily yield a discovery. "Foul : Free throw" passes it.

provenance.note: Max's most common reason for killing a set. Twice he supplied the fix himself (Player : Jersey, Hiking : Summit). The examples in the text are his own words.

rules.text: Word familiarity affects difficulty: the relationship and the words together set a set's difficulty. A green set must use words the average person knows without thinking; obscure words raise the difficulty regardless of how simple the relationship is.

provenance.note: The green slot kept landing too hard because the rater grades relationship trickiness alone. Wording is Max's amendment: familiarity AFFECTS difficulty, it does not replace the relationship as the driver.
